newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee reverses direction, mostly down.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee reverses direction, mostly down.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures, tracking lower New York values, reversed their early uptrend to end Monday mostly down on light trade and origin selling.
But benchmark May managed to close unchanged at $1,690 a tonne after falling to an intraday low of $1,680. It hit a high of $1,705.
Other traded positions were $6 to $14 down.
The day's volume was a meagre 4,032 lots. May/July switches were earlier traded at $10.
Traders did not detect any speculative or fund participation.
All eyes remained glued on New York arabica market which saw benchmark May falling back after a sharply higher close on Friday.
The contract dipped to a session low of 177.30 cents a lb before trading at 180.75 by 1724 GMT, still 5.60 cents down.

Traders said New York looked vulnerable to further losses if May makes persistent assault at below 178 cents a lb, as this could trigger fund sell-stops. But roaster short-covering could provide some support at the lows.
LIFFE said after the close of the morning trade that certified stocks held at its nominated warehouses fell slightly to 2,801 five-tonne lots in February from 2,831 in January.
Friday's CFTC Commitment of Traders report which showed net speculative long positions of 14,448 lots as at March 11 was seen as neutral.
"There was a sizeable speculative activity on Thursday and Friday which obviously was not reflected in the report," said one trader.

The market is awaiting Green Coffee Association of New York's monthly stock data due after the close of New York trading on Monday. Traders said the stocks are expected to show an increase of 50,000 to 100,000 bags.
New York's spot March expires on Tuesday. By the close of business of Friday, New York's Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange reported certified coffee stocks reached 44,483 60-kg bags as of March 13.

There were an additional 27,946 bags pending grading. Broker GNI said traders should note that a large proportion of these are in New Orleans, where the last lot graded had a rejection rate of over 75 percent.
